title: EU AI Act Article 4 -- AI Literacy Obligations Every Deployer Must Meet
context: 2026-08-14 -- GPAI obligations fully enforceable since 2 Aug 2026; Article 4 AI-literacy duty now binding on providers and deployers
body: Article 4 of the EU AI Act imposes a standing obligation on both providers and deployers to ensure a sufficient level of AI literacy among staff who operate or use AI systems. This is not a one-time training checkbox: it is a continuous duty that scales with the risk tier of the system and the role of each employee. For deployers of high-risk systems, this means documentation of who operates the system, what they were trained on, and when — evidence a market surveillance authority can request. Practically, organisations should (1) map every human-in-the-loop role to a training record, (2) maintain role-specific AI literacy curricula updated to the systems capability and misuse modes, and (3) keep auditable proof that training predates deployment. The Council of AI treats AI literacy as part of its measurement board: a governance axis score reflects whether an operator can correctly interpret a measurement credential, recognise a monitored-containment boundary, and escalate a suspected escape. Measured assurance applies to people, not just models.
